name: Latvia
convention: Statutory work-free holidays per 'Par svētku, atceres un atzīmējamām dienām' (likumi.lv, fetched directly — primary source). Includes the always-Sunday statutory holidays (Easter Sunday, Pentecost), flagged in notes. KEY FEATURE: a statutory substitute-day rule — when May 4 (Restoration of Independence Declaration Day), November 18 (Proclamation Day), or the Song & Dance Festival closing day falls on a weekend, the FOLLOWING WORKING DAY is a day off. That is the observance 'nextWorkingDay' as data, and 2025-05-05 below is a live instance of it. Easter Monday IS a holiday (unlike Estonia).

confidence.2025: HIGH — primary statute + substitute-day clause applied (2025-05-04 is a Sunday → 2025-05-05 substitute confirmed by the clause)
confidence.2026: HIGH — primary statute; no substitute days arise (May 4 Mon, Nov 18 Wed)
confidence.2027: HIGH — primary statute; no substitute days arise (May 4 Tue, Nov 18 Thu)

notes: 2025-05-05 is the substitute Monday for 2025-05-04 (Sunday); the nominal day stays listed (it is still the holiday) and the substitute is an additional non-working day — the exact shape the per-holiday observance field must produce.
Always-Sunday entries: Easter Sunday and Pentecost (2025-06-08, 2026-05-24, 2027-05-16). Other weekend-falling: 2026-12-26 (Sat), 2027-05-01 (Sat), 2027-12-25 (Sat), 2027-12-26 (Sun).
